$comment: Parity policy for the shared VfAvatar cases. Plain data: no DSL, no waiver engine. The one component in M16 whose contract is an ordering rather than a mapping, and the one that renders through the neutral icon registry.

classifications.exact: Must match literally across every target. Structure, canonical classes, native attributes, visible text, accessible names, computed geometry and colour.
classifications.semantic: Framework mechanics may differ; the observable meaning must not. How content is composed, how a renderer marks its own output.
classifications.framework-specific: Historical behaviour of one adapter that the other is not required to reproduce. Narrow, named, and covered by its own test.

notCompared.$comment: Recorded so a reviewer can see what is deliberately outside the comparison, without leaving dead dimensions that look like live protection. Nothing here is a waiver: the extractor never produces these differences in the first place.
notCompared.attributeOrder: Attributes are extracted into a sorted map, so serialisation order cannot produce a difference. It carries no meaning.
notCompared.rendererMarkers: Vue scope attributes (data-v-*) and the Razor ownership marker (data-vf-razor*) are dropped by scripts/parity/extract.mjs. They identify the renderer, not the product. Any other data-* attribute is compared as dom.productData.

dom.structure.description: An unexpected element, invalid wrapper arrangement, or tag mismatch. Never approvable; comparison continues through tag differences so meaningful attribute/child diagnostics remain visible.

dom.canonicalClasses.description: vf-* classes on every element. Consumer classes included, because where a consumer class lands relative to the canonical ones is part of the contract.

dom.nativeAttributes.description: class and style on the root span, the src and alt of the image branch, and the glyph's own svg attributes. alt is the contract rather than incidental markup: it is always written, and its default empty value is what makes the image decorative.

dom.text.description: Visible text content of every element.

dom.aria.description: aria-* attributes and role. The avatar writes none of its own; the only ARIA it emits is the aria-hidden on the glyph, which is why an icon-only avatar has no accessible name.

dom.productData.description: data-* attributes that belong to the product rather than to a renderer.

style.geometry.description: Computed box metrics of every measured role.

style.colour.description: Computed colour, background and border colour of every measured role.

visual.description: Rendered screenshot of the case, per theme.

a11y.role.description: The role each measured node exposes in the accessibility tree, including exposing none.

a11y.name.description: The accessible name each measured node exposes, including exposing none.

a11y.states.description: Accessibility states exposed by each measured node.

static.noInteraction.description: The recorded fact that the component declares no interaction to drive, and that the harness measured this rather than skipping the stage. Includes the component-owned focusable and interactive-role counts, which for an avatar are zero on every target.

historicalQuirks.description: image -> label -> icon -> default slot, decided by v-if/v-else-if. A reordering renders an avatar for every input, so nothing about the result looks wrong.
historicalQuirks.reason: The single most plausible port defect in M16. Every branch and every adjacent pair has its own case.

historicalQuirks.description: The tests are plain truthiness, so image="" falls through to the label exactly as an absent image does, and there is no way to request an empty label.
historicalQuirks.reason: Switching to a presence test would render an empty img or an empty label span where the reference renders the next branch.

historicalQuirks.description: imageAlt defaults to '' rather than to undefined, so the image branch always carries an alt attribute. A missing alt and an empty one are different things to a screen reader.
historicalQuirks.reason: Dropping the attribute would turn every unlabelled avatar into an unlabelled image announced by its filename.

historicalQuirks.description: VueIconify sets inheritAttrs: false and spreads its attrs onto the inner svg, so class="vf-avatar__icon" reaches the glyph rather than the wrapper span, and so does aria-hidden.
historicalQuirks.reason: Not a decision this component made, but one it depends on: the avatar stylesheet sizes .vf-avatar__icon, and moving it to the wrapper would size the wrong box.

historicalQuirks.description: The size modifier is suppressed by comparing against md; the shape modifier exists only for circle. square is not the value the shape modifier is named after.
historicalQuirks.reason: Folding them into one 'suppress the default' loop is the obvious simplification and emits vf-avatar--square, which no stylesheet defines.

historicalQuirks.description: The Vue icon component silently substitutes a placeholder glyph for a name it does not know; the neutral Razor registry throws. No case exercises an unknown name, so no comparison depends on this.
historicalQuirks.reason: It is a property of the icon packages, not of VfAvatar, and reconciling it would change the icon contract for every component rather than for this one. Recorded rather than approved: there is no divergence to approve, because no case produces one.
